input:
For x > 1, if (2x)^(2y) = 4e^(2x-2y), then (1 + log 2x)² · dy/dx is equal to

Options:
A. (x log 2x + log 2)/x
B. (x log 2x - log 2)/x
C. x log 2x
D. log 2x

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given the implicit relation (2x)^(2y) = 4e^(2x-2y) for x > 1, take the logarithm to express y explicitly, differentiate with respect to x, and find the value of (1 + log 2x)² · dy/dx.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Taking log on both sides linearises the exponents. After simplification, y can be expressed as y = (x + log 2)/(1 + log 2x), and then standard quotient rule gives dy/dx.

key_concepts: Logarithm of a power: log(A^n) = n log A

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Take logarithm of both sides, simplify to express y = (x + log 2)/(1 + log 2x), then differentiate using the quotient rule, and multiply both sides by (1 + log 2x)² to get the required expression.
logical_steps: Step 1: Take log on both sides of (2x)^(2y) = 4e^(2x-2y)
Step 2: Expand and collect y terms
Step 3: Isolate y to get y = (x + log 2)/(1 + log 2x)
Step 5: Multiply through by (1 + log 2x)² and simplify

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: y = (x+log2)/(1+log2x). By quotient rule, numerator of dy/dx = (1+log2x)·1 - (x+log2)·(1/x) = log2x - log2/x = (x log2x - log2)/x. Multiplying by (1+log2x)² gives the required expression ✓
